facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against treating integration as the main risk is operating: utilization, rental revenue growth and twice-raised 2026 guidance suggest the combined fleet is earning more per dollar of cost, and the near-term notes were replaced at par rather than through an exchange. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the earnings trajectory: last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 16.53% in six months, the third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin reached 44.2%, the issuer raised 2026 guidance for the second time this year and replaced its 2027 notes at par. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Herc's net debt is 4.12x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at September 30, 2026, above the 3.90x the issuer reports because its figure rests on adjusted, pro forma earnings, so creditors should size leverage on the higher reported measure.
Basis: calculation C27; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4

Leverage has fallen from 4.79x at March 31 to 4.27x at June 30 and 4.12x at September 30, but the fall comes from earnings, not repayment: net debt is broadly flat at USD 7,942 million, USD 7,869 million and USD 7,965 million while last-twelve-months EBITDA rose from USD 1,658 million to USD 1,932 million as H&E rolled into the base.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C27; calculation C8; calculation C12
Liquidity is USD 2,100 million, almost all undrawn asset-based revolver, and the USD 550 million AR Facility is fully drawn and falls due on August 31, 2027, inside twelve months.
Basis: calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18
### Analysis by dimension

The H&E acquisition, completed on June 2, 2025, roughly doubled carrying debt from USD 4,086 million at year-end 2024 to USD 8,047 million at year-end 2025, which lifted net debt over fiscal-year EBITDA from 2.95x to 5.34x. The 5.34x overstates run-rate leverage because it sets full year-end debt against seven months of acquired earnings, so only the last-twelve-months ratios at June 30 and September 30, 2026 are comparable with each other. Within them the improvement to 4.12x is earnings-led: net debt moved from USD 7,942 million at March 31 to USD 7,965 million at September 30.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

EBITDA covered cash interest 3.65x over the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, after 3.99x at March 31 and 3.47x at June 30; the dip in June reflects the H&E financing entering the trailing cash-interest window in full before earnings caught up. Cash interest paid is USD 67 million below interest expense, net, in nine months 2026, and cover here uses cash paid.
Basis: calculation C22; calculation C25; calculation C28; calculation C45

Operating cash flow of USD 951 million in nine months 2026 did not cover USD 1,056 million of rental equipment expenditure without USD 319 million of disposal proceeds. Before disposals, operating cash flow less capital expenditure was negative USD 212 million, and the issuer's free cash flow of USD 133 million depends on USD 345 million of disposal proceeds. Dividends paid of USD 71 million took more than half of that free cash flow, and receivables absorbed USD 260 million as revenue grew.
Basis: calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 66 million of cash and USD 2,034 million available under the asset-based revolver, which matures on June 2, 2030. The AR Facility is fully drawn, so its extension in August 2026 to August 31, 2027 is the nearest refinancing event. The issuer states no ongoing financial maintenance covenant; a fixed charge coverage test applies only if liquidity falls below levels that are not printed.
Basis: calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Three definition choices move the numbers and each is carried both ways. Net debt on carrying value is USD 7,965 million against USD 8,014 million on principal; financing obligations of USD 97 million sit outside Total Debt; and the issuer's 3.90x net leverage uses pro forma adjusted EBITDA that is not printed, so its 0.22x gap to the reported 4.12x cannot be decomposed. The ladder of maturities is dated December 31, 2025 and does not say where the AR Facility sits.
Basis: calculation C47; calculation C48; calculation C40; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the earnings trend: adjusted EBITDA reached USD 603 million in the third quarter and the issuer raised 2026 guidance for the second time this year, which, if sustained with flat net debt, lowers reported leverage further. The view would weaken if net rental capital expenditure, guided to USD 1.0 billion to USD 1.1 billion for the year against USD 737 million spent in nine months, is funded by borrowing rather than disposals, or if the utilization gains reverse.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

## Findings
### Bottom line

Herc is a diversified, scaled equipment-rental business whose credit risk now rests on integrating the debt-funded H&E acquisition rather than on its market position; no controlling holder is disclosed and the dividend continues, so creditor protection comes from performance, not sponsor support.

The acquisition, completed on June 2, 2025 for a total purchase price of USD 4.8 billion, nearly doubled carrying debt in 2025 and added branches in over 30 U.S. states; management says integration finished in the first quarter of 2026 but publishes no integration cost or synergy amount. Demand is spread: no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue and national accounts are 49%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_herc2026q1-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C17

The USD 0.70 quarterly dividend continued through the acquisition year, and the ownership and compensation detail that would show who controls the company sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
### Key findings

- The business is scaled and diversified, which supports cash-flow resilience through the cycle. Contractors, industrial, infrastructure and government, commercial facilities and other customers account for 38%, 25%, 18%, 14% and 5% of equipment rental revenue, national accounts for 49%, and no customer exceeds 3%. Equipment rental is 86.15% of FY2025 revenue and the only segment, so fleet utilization and rental rates drive almost all earnings.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C1

- The H&E acquisition is the dominant credit event, and its delivery matters more than business quality. The USD 4.8 billion purchase was funded by USD 2.8 billion of new senior unsecured notes, a USD 750 million term loan and USD 2.5 billion drawn on a new revolver, and new Herc shares valued at USD 584 million went to H&E holders. Management says integration finished in the first quarter of 2026 and synergies are tracking to plan, but integration cost and synergy amounts are not disclosed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_herc2026q1-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_herc2026q2-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Ownership and control give creditors neither a sponsor to lean on nor a sponsor to fear. No holder above reporting thresholds is named, the chairman is non-executive and the annual report incorporates holdings, compensation and related-party detail by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a controlling holder is not ruled out.

- Capital allocation is mixed rather than extractive. The dividend of USD 0.70 per share each quarter continued while debt rose, but there were no repurchases in 2025, disposal and refinancing proceeds went to debt, and the 2027 notes were redeemed at par. Dividends paid of USD 71 million in the first nine months of 2026 equal 53.38% of the issuer's free cash flow.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C12

- Leased branches and a fixed cost base amplify cyclical risk. About 94% of locations are leased, operating lease liabilities of USD 1,502 million sit outside debt, rental contracts can be cancelled within a day, and rent, insurance and overhead do not fall in the winter, so a demand slowdown reaches cash flow faster than the revenue mix suggests.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Operating momentum is strong but largely acquired. Equipment rental revenue rose 21.09% in the first nine months of 2026 and dollar utilization reached 43.5% in the third quarter against 39.9%, yet direct operating costs rose to 44.6% of equipment rental revenue in the nine months, and organic growth is not separated from acquired growth.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C19
- Legal exposure looks ordinary-course on the evidence supplied: claims arise from operating rented equipment and workers' compensation, and management does not expect a material adverse effect.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against treating integration as the main risk is operating: utilization, rental revenue growth and twice-raised 2026 guidance suggest the combined fleet is earning more per dollar of cost, and the near-term notes were replaced at par rather than through an exchange. The view would soften if cross-selling and branch optimization lift margins as management says and synergy amounts are disclosed; it would harden if integration costs recur, organic growth proves weak once acquired revenue is removed, or the dividend and fleet investment are funded by borrowing.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104
### Limitations
- The ownership conclusion changes if the proxy statement shows a holder with influence over distributions, because the finding that sponsor extraction risk is absent would no longer hold.
- The integration conclusion rests on management statements; disclosed integration costs or a synergy shortfall would raise or lower the weight given to delivery risk.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-28_herc2026q1-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_herc2026q2-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Funding mix and restricted-payment capacity are read from filing summaries, not executed agreements, so the judgement that capital allocation is mixed rather than extractive could change once the agreements are read.
- Customer and end-market shares are for FY2025 only; a shift toward project-heavy national accounts after the acquisition would change the diversification conclusion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On June 2, 2025 Herc completed its acquisition of H&E Equipment Services, a full-service rental company with branches in over 30 U.S. states, for a total purchase price of USD 4.8 billion, made up of USD 2.9 billion of cash and new Herc shares valued at USD 584 million, and paid a further USD 1.4 billion in cash to extinguish H&E debt that was not assumed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C16

Herc funded the deal with USD 2.8 billion of new senior unsecured notes due 2030 and 2033, a USD 750 million term loan and USD 2.5 billion drawn on a new asset-based revolver of up to USD 4.0 billion, of which about USD 1.6 billion repaid the prior revolver, so carrying debt nearly doubled in 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114–116; calculation C17

In December 2025 Herc redeemed the USD 1.2 billion 2027 notes at par using the proceeds of USD 600 million each of new 2031 and 2034 senior notes, and it cut the term loan margin; the AR Facility was amended four times between August 2025 and August 2026 and now stands at USD 550 million, due on August 31, 2027.

Herc sold its Cinelease studio entertainment business on July 31, 2025 for USD 100 million of initial cash plus earnouts and used the proceeds to repay debt, and in 2024 it bought the assets of Otay Mesa Sales for about USD 273 million. The documents describe no pending acquisition and no new debt issue after the third quarter of 2026.

# Fundamental credit: HERC HOLDINGS INC (hri), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

HERC HOLDINGS INC (issuer id hri), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the business, financial and governance evidence into a fundamental credit view. It assigns no rating and makes no recommendation.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Herc's fundamental credit profile is adequate: a scaled, diversified fleet business whose net leverage of 4.12x on reported last-twelve-months EBITDA is elevated and falls only through earnings growth, leaving creditors reliant on cash flow, an asset-backed revolver and disposals rather than sponsor support.
Basis: calculation C1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The main support is spread: no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue, liquidity is USD 2,100 million with USD 2,034 million available under a revolver due 2030, and last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 16.53% from March to September 2026. The main constraint is cash generation: issuer free cash flow of USD 133 million includes USD 345 million of disposal proceeds, and the fully drawn USD 550 million AR Facility matures on August 31, 2027.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

The primary downside path is a construction slowdown that cuts utilization while rent, insurance and overhead stay fixed, which would raise leverage on flat debt; the monitor is net leverage on reported EBITDA moving above 4.12x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C1
### Key findings

- Scale and customer spread are the main credit support. No customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue, national accounts are 49%, and equipment rental is the only segment, so weakness in one end market is diluted across contractors, industrial, infrastructure and commercial facilities customers.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Leverage is the main constraint and is falling through earnings, not repayment. Net debt is 4.12x reported last-twelve-months EBITDA and total debt 4.16x at September 30, 2026, against 3.90x reported by the issuer on adjusted pro forma earnings; the ratio was 4.79x at March 31 and 4.27x at June 30 while carrying net debt at September 30 was only USD 23 million above its March 31 level.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Interest absorbs much of the earnings gain. EBITDA covers cash interest 3.65x over the last twelve months, cash interest paid rose 54.95% in nine months 2026 as the acquisition financing ran for a full period, and the floating-rate revolver and term loan keep it sensitive to rates.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

- Free cash flow is thin and disposal-dependent. Issuer free cash flow of USD 133 million for nine months 2026 includes USD 345 million of disposal proceeds; before them operating cash flow less capital expenditure is negative USD 212 million, and dividends of USD 71 million take 53.38% of the issuer figure.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Liquidity is adequate for now and the nearest refinancing is the AR Facility. Cash plus revolver availability is USD 2,100 million, 3.96x last-twelve-months cash interest; the AR Facility of USD 550 million is fully drawn and due on August 31, 2027, and the largest principal bucket, 45.82% of the December 31, 2025 ladder, falls in 2030.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

- Governance and financial policy are mixed rather than adverse. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, the dividend of USD 0.70 per share continues and the acquisition was debt-funded; capacity under the debt agreements is unread, so willingness and capacity to extract value are both unevidenced.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53

- Margins face cost pressure that the issuer ties to the acquisition, fuel and delivery. Direct operating expense was 44.63% of equipment rental revenue in nine months 2026 against 42.95%, while the issuer's adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 41.5% from 41.0%.
Basis: calculation C16; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- Integration is reported complete but cannot be verified. Management says synergies are tracking to plan, and no integration cost or synergy amount is disclosed, so the earnings gain cannot yet be split between synergies, organic demand and acquired revenue.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-07-28_herc2026q2-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the earnings trajectory: last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 16.53% in six months, the third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin reached 44.2%, the issuer raised 2026 guidance for the second time this year and replaced its 2027 notes at par. If net debt stays flat and EBITDA keeps growing, reported leverage would keep falling toward the issuer's 3.90x. The view would improve if free cash flow before disposals turned positive and synergy amounts were disclosed; it would worsen if utilization or rental rates fell, if disposal proceeds weakened, or if the AR Facility were not extended well ahead of August 31, 2027.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C18; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104
### Limitations

- Reported leverage is built from filed figures; an issuer-adjusted trailing EBITDA, which is not supplied, would lower the ratio and could move the assessment of leverage tolerance from constrained toward adequate.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4

- No rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so the judgement that leverage is elevated is absolute, not relative to comparable issuers, and the access-to-markets view rests on past issuance alone.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- The refinancing view uses a maturity ladder dated December 31, 2025; a ladder at September 30, 2026 could change the size and timing of near-term maturities.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104
- The downside scenario is qualitative because no management case, sensitivity or executed covenant terms are supplied, so liquidity runway under stress is not quantified.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths are scale, spread and access. Scale and market position are average, with an estimated 4% market share in a fragmented industry; business diversification is strong because no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue and national accounts are 49%; the ability to refinance is average, supported by the redemption of the 2027 notes at par with new 2031 and 2034 notes and by USD 2.8 billion of 2030 and 2033 notes issued in 2025, but untested by rating or price evidence; liquidity is strong at USD 2,100 million, with the revolver due in 2030.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; calculation C8

Weaknesses are cash generation and cost. Free cash flow stability is weak because issuer free cash flow depends on USD 345 million of disposal proceeds; margin stability and cost flexibility are average, since direct operating expense rose to 44.63% of equipment rental revenue while rent, insurance and overhead are fixed; competitive advantage is average, resting on scale and national accounts rather than contracts, as virtually all rentals can be cancelled within a day; financial policy and governance are average, with a debt-funded acquisition, a continuing dividend and no sponsor to backstop equity.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A)
